subject: Post-demo: secure-link onboarding & network action items
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@acloudsys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: secure-link onboarding & network action items

Hi Samira — thanks again for the demo time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get your network team unblocked: 

Summary (30 min demo)
- Walked through Redwood Hosted API + private VPC endpoint options and SDK quickstart.
- Showed structured output and tool-calling flow for your ingestion pipeline.
- Discussed embeddings + reranker approach for semantic search and latency trade-offs.

Network/Connectivity items we need from you to finalize sandbox access:
1) Preferred connectivity model: VPC endpoint (recommended) or IP allowlist. If VPC endpoint, confirm cloud provider (I believe AWS) and VPC ID.
2) If IP allowlist: please provide firewall contact and the public egress IPs (we'll supply Redwood's outbound ranges).
3) DNS: do you prefer a private hosted zone (Route 53 private hosted zone) or split-horizon DNS?
4) mTLS: If you require mutual TLS for control-plane auth, let us know your cert rotation cadence and CA (internal CA or public).
5) Proxy/egress: confirm whether your egress goes through a corporate proxy and whether SNI passthrough is allowed.

Next steps
- Priyom is looping in on the technical details and will drop a short checklist and connector config for your infra team (see attachment).
- Can we schedule a 30-minute networking touchpoint with your NetOps next week? We have Tue/Wed 10–12 PT open.

Attachments: redwood_sdk_quickstart.md (quickstart), networking_requirements.csv (matrix of ports, IPs, DNS entries)

Thanks — happy to keep this lightweight.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Thanks Laura — great walkthrough. Looping in our NetOps alias for details. Quick answers from our side and a couple of follow-ups: 

- Cloud: AWS, account 111222333, VPC vpc-0a1b2c3d (we can share a cross-account role if needed).
- Preferred: VPC endpoint (we prefer not to open many public IPs).
- DNS: we use Route 53 private hosted zones; would prefer Redwood to support a private CNAME for the endpoint.
- mTLS: we require mutual TLS for all management/control connections; our security team uses an internal CA with quarterly rotation. Can Redwood accept client certs issued by our internal CA?
- Proxy: our egress flows through a corporate proxy for egress filtering; we'll confirm whether SNI passthrough is allowed.

Also, we need to confirm whether embeddings requests and reranker calls can be routed through the same VPC endpoint or if they require separate endpoints due to different model routings. If you can summarize that in the checklist, that would help with procurement.

Can do Tue 10 PT for the NetOps quick call — Samira and one of our infra engineers will join.

Thanks,
Samira

samira@acloudsys.com

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Hi Samira — thanks for the quick answers, and appreciated the VPC details. A few technical clarifications to help your NetOps team plan the firewall and DNS changes: 

Technical checklist (high level)
- Single VPC endpoint: embeddings, generation, and reranker traffic can use the same private endpoint. We surface model routing via path-based routes; routing to different model backends occurs inside Redwood and does not require extra endpoints.
- Ports & protocols: outbound/inbound use HTTPS (443). We do not require additional TCP ports for inference traffic.
- IP ranges: for initial sandbox we can give a small set of egress IPs; for production we recommend an interface VPC endpoint and cross-account role.
- DNS: support private CNAME to our internal endpoint; we'll provide the canonical target (eg endpoint.redwood-internal.net).
- mTLS/auth: two options depending on your preference:
  * API-key + TLS (standard): client uses SDK with an API key over TLS; easiest for quick proof-of-concept.
  * mTLS (control plane): we can accept client certs signed by your internal CA if you expose the CA chain and the cert subject mapping. We support cert rotation; recommend a 90-day rotation window.
- Certificate format: PEM is preferred. If you have certs in JKS we can accept them after conversion.
- Proxy considerations: if your egress terminates TLS at the proxy (TLS interception), please ensure the proxy allows SNI passthrough to preserve routing or provide a proxy TLS cert that matches the SNI expected by Redwood.
- Structured output/tool-calling: webhook callbacks for tool calling will originate from the same endpoint; if you plan to receive callbacks inside your VPC, confirm a reachable address or LB with an open port 443.

Attachments included in this thread:
- redwood_sdk_quickstart.md (contains SDK snippets for API key & mTLS examples)
- networking_requirements.csv (CSV with IP ranges, DNS names, and port matrix)

Action items
- Laura: schedule Tue 10 PT NetOps touchpoint (Samira confirmed).
- Samira: share NetOps engineer email + security contact (for cert signing/rotation process).
- Priyom/Ben: provide sandbox egress IPs and endpoint canonical name before the call.

If useful, I can prepare a short runbook for cert rotation and a Terraform snippet for the VPC endpoint during the call.

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai
